validity.recommendation: No fabrication risk — the underlying transmission network and its operator/owner are well documented in an independent SEC 10-K and the current parent-company's operations page. But no independent source anywhere (SEC filing, TriSummit/ENSTAR materials, NPMS) uses the specific name 'Anchorage System' or attests a discrete 50-mile segment boundary — treat LengthKnown (50.00 mi) as unverified at the segment level until a PHMSA NPMS county-map export or an RCA/DNR filing that actually names this segment is located.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/ATTRIBUTION checked independently of GEM. The sheet's current [ref] for Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Location is the bare NPMS root (https://www.npms.phmsa.dot.gov/) — confirmed by direct fetch (HTTP 200, 17KB landing page: PIMMA login, Public Map Viewer link, About/FAQ) to contain zero pipeline-specific content; it is a navigation surface, not a citation (matches this batch's addendum finding — same defect on 44 units across 11 rows in this slice). The Owner [ref] (ENSTAR March-2022 PDF) was independently re-extracted with pdftotext -layout: it describes ENSTAR owning/operating 'over 400 miles of high-pressure natural gas transmission pipelines in Southcentral Alaska' ranging 2-20in diameter at 270-1000+ PSI, but the literal phrase 'Anchorage System' does not appear anywhere in it (0 hits on grep) — the worklist's own existing_ref_checks flag of name_found=true/name_matched='Anchorage System Gas Pipeline' on this ref is a FALSE POSITIVE from the builder's fuzzy matcher (it is loosely matching the generic tokens 'Anchorage' and 'System' rather than the phrase); corrected to name_found=false in this shard's Owner fill. Independent corroboration found instead: SEC EDGAR full-text search located SEMCO Energy Inc's FY2005 10-K (CIK 0000277158, filed 2006-03-14, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277158/000095012406001183/k02906e10vk.htm), which describes 'Alaska Pipeline Company' (APC) as a real subsidiary whose 'transmission system delivers natural gas from producing fields in South Central Alaska to ENSTAR's Anchorage-area gas distribution system... APC's only customer is ENSTAR', with the network at ~393 miles of gas transmission pipeline in 2005 — this directly confirms the sheet's Operator value 'Alaska Pipeline Co LLC' as a genuine, historically documented entity feeding gas specifically into Anchorage, and confirms Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission, and general Location=Anchorage/Alaska as categorical facts about the shared network. TriSummit's current ENSTAR operations page (https://trisummit.ca/operations/enstar-natural-gas, verified live) independently confirms ENSTAR Natural Gas Co as the current owner/operator, 'headquartered in Anchorage, Alaska', '711 kilometers of high-pressure transmission lines... two subsea pipelines that deliver gas from the Kenai Gas Fields to Anchorage and beyond' — i.e. a present-day, larger (711km/442mi) version of the same network. NONE of these three sources uses the phrase 'Anchorage System' or gives a 50-mile figure for a segment of that name. CROSS-CHECK: summing the LengthKnown values of the other APC/ENSTAR-affiliated Alaska rows on this roster (P7450, P7453, P7454, P7455, P7456, P7458, P7461 — excluding P7462 Nuiqsut/Alpine and P7465 Trans-Alaska/TAPS fuel-gas, which are different operators/systems) plus this row's 50 mi gives ~378.55 mi, remarkably close to the SEC 10-K's 2005 total (~393 mi) and TriSummit's current total (~442 mi/711 km) — strong circumstantial evidence that GEM's Alaska roster is a legitimate, if internally-drawn, decomposition of one real, continuously-documented transmission network into individually named system/segment rows, not a fabricated entity. Net call: real infrastructure, correctly classified and attributed; the caveat is narrowly that the specific 'Anchorage System' segment identity/boundary/length is GEM's own decomposition, unattested by any outside source found. ACCESS CORRECTION (2026-09-15 re-audit): the prior pass's blocked-source claims were partly false and are restated here. rca.alaska.gov LIVE genuinely 403s: reproduced with curl (browser UA, --compressed) -> HTTP 403, 'Server: DataDome' / 'X-DataDome: protected', 773-byte challenge page. But Wayback is NOT empty for this host -- the prior claim of 'zero snapshots' was false: CDX lists thousands of captures back to 2004. The 2026-08-14 capture of the site root (web.archive.org/web/20260814171212/https://rca.alaska.gov/) redirects to the pre-2020 RCAWeb/home.aspx template and returns real page content (menus, docket/meeting links), not a JS shell. A 2005 capture of rca.alaska.gov/data/companyDetail.html?acronym=ENSTAR (200, real content) is an actual RCA 'Company: ENSTAR' record: CPCN #4 ('ENSTAR NATURAL GAS COMPANY, A DIVISION OF SEMCO', Gas) plus a docket history including U-01-007 'ALASKA PIPELINE COMPANY AND UNION OIL COMPANY OF CALIFORNIA, GAS SALES AGMT' (2001) and U-00-088 'ENSTAR NATURAL GAS CO. & ALASKA PIPELINE CO., INVE[STIGATION]' (2000) -- independent state-regulator confirmation of the APC/ENSTAR relationship already established via the SEC 10-K. It is a company/docket index, though, not a segment record: no mileage, diameter, capacity, pressure, or construction/proposal/start date for any specific segment, and it does not name 'Anchorage System.' Not every RCA capture is usable, and that cuts the other way too: a same-day (2026-08-14) capture of a different current-site page (ForConsumers/NaturalGas.aspx) IS a DataDome JS-challenge shell (403, ~2.4KB) -- captures on this domain are page/timestamp-dependent, so neither 'no snapshots exist' nor 'everything is a JS shell' is accurate. A direct lookup of ENSTAR's own certificate detail page (data/certificateDetail.html?CPCN=4, the record most likely to carry system extent) returns Wayback 404 -- genuinely not archived, not a block.
Alaska DNR (dog.dnr.alaska.gov) is NOT blocked -- the prior note's '403 behind a DataDome bot-challenge' claim was false. Reproduced live 2026-09-15: the site root and /Services/Pipelines both return HTTP 200 with real content; only the guessed singular path /Services/Pipeline (no trailing pipeline name) 404s -- a bad URL, not a block. The correct listing (dog.dnr.alaska.gov/Services/Pipelines) was read in full: it names every DNR/State Pipeline Coordinator-regulated line (TAPS, Alaska Stand Alone Pipeline, Alpine Diesel/Oil/Utility, Badami, CIGGS, Donlin, Endicott, Kenai Kachemak, Kuparuk, Liberty, Milne Point, Nikiski Alaska, North Fork, Northstar Gas/Oil, Nuiqsut Natural Gas, Oliktok Natural Gas, Pebble, Pikka, Point Thomson, Tyonek W 10 Gas, Willow, WNS Products/Utility) -- none named 'Anchorage System,' 'ENSTAR,' or 'Alaska Pipeline Company.' This is a genuine, reproducible negative finding, not an access failure: DNR's State Pipeline Coordinator's Section leases rights-of-way to common/contract-carrier pipelines on state land (overwhelmingly North Slope oil/gas + TAPS + a few Cook Inlet industrial lines) -- a different regulatory track from the RCA-certificated public gas utility (ENSTAR/APC) that serves this segment. This network falls outside DNR's registry by jurisdiction, not by blockage. No EIA match either (checked sources/eia_pipeline_projects/data/eia_projects_long.csv directly for 'anchorage'/'alaska pipeline'/'enstar'; all 28 hits are the unrelated ASAP project, P0293's row). No FERC docket applies (state-regulated utility, not FERC-jurisdictional). Genuinely nothing states a proposal year for this specific 50-mile segment -- left blank rather than forced.
